raw_comment:
I notice that the coastal areas on the map experience less intense droughts, while the landlocked states in the central part of the country are hit the hardest. Although the intensity is greater in the center, some coastal states are still affected by drought.

I wonder why certain areas are completely free from drought. This is puzzling because these spots appear scattered across the country, even near regions experiencing severe drought conditions. Additionally, I’m curious why Alaska seems to be entirely unaffected by drought.

This issue is personal to me because I have family in west Texas who often talk about the drought and its impact. It’s a serious problem that affects much of the country in one way or another.

Arid regions scattered across the country.
